fragments.title: Incident Report — VALE-7
fragments.content:
AUDITCORP SECURITY DIVISION // INCIDENT REPORT

REPORT NUMBER: IR-0441-[REDACTED]
OPERATOR: VALE-7 (Callum)
DATE: [REDACTED]
SHIFT: 22:00 — 06:00
LOCATION ASSIGNED: Server Wing East — Corridor B
SUPERVISOR: [SIGNATURE ABSENT]

I remained at my post in the server wing for the duration of my shift. I did notice a significant spill of industrial solvent in Corridor B at approximately 02:30. I attempted to flag it for janitorial services but did not leave the restricted zone. My sleeve may have come into contact with the residue while I was checking the perimeter.

No individuals entered or exited the restricted zone during my watch. No anomalies were observed. No alarms were triggered in my section during the period in question.

The 40-minute gap in surveillance footage is consistent with the scheduled maintenance window logged by the systems team on the same date. This is a known issue and has been documented by facility IT on previous occasions.

I did not file a request for footage review as I did not consider it necessary. My account is complete.

I have nothing further to add.

— VALE-7

COUNTER-SIGNATURE (Supervisor): _______________
STATUS: UNSIGNED

fragments.title: Medical Bay Corridor — 02:52
fragments.content:
Security camera still — medical bay hallway, timestamp 02:52:14. Subject identified as VALE-7. Seated on floor, back against wall, left of medical bay door. 

In his right hand, he is holding a bright orange identification badge—standard issue for temporary janitorial staff. He appears to be inspecting the name on the badge while looking toward the door. 

NOTE: Transit time on foot from the Server Wing to this location is a minimum of 4 minutes. 
NOTE: The Server Wing access log (Fragment-02) recorded this subject at 02:51:12. This still is timestamped 02:52:14. Elapsed time: 62 seconds. 
NOTE: It is physically impossible to traverse 340 meters in 62 seconds while stopping to assist a collapsed individual.

fragments.title: Medical Bay Intake Log
fragments.content:
AUDITCORP MEDICAL BAY // INTAKE LOG

TIMESTAMP: 02:52:41
ATTENDING: DR. OSEI (on-call)
ESCORTING OFFICER: VALE-7 — did not enter bay, waited in corridor
CASE REF: MB-[REDACTED]-NID

INITIAL PRESENTATION:
Unknown individual, female, approx. 30-35 years. Brought to medical bay by facility guard following collapse in sub-level corridor B. Guard reported subject fell without warning. Guard waited outside the bay for the duration of treatment and did not enter.

Individual was non-responsive on arrival. No ID presented. No corporate employee number on file. Clothing consistent with cleaning or maintenance staff.

CLINICAL NOTES:
Signs of dehydration. Minor abrasion on right temple consistent with a fall — impact with floor or wall surface. No fractures observed. No signs of pre-existing injury.

Treatment administered: IV fluids, observation. Individual stabilised within 20 minutes. Responsive and oriented by 03:18. Escorted off-site at 04:00 by unknown individual — not by the facility guard on duty.

ATTENDING NOTE (Dr. Osei):
The guard who brought her in — VALE-7 — was still in the hallway when I stepped out at 03:22. He asked only if she was going to be alright. He did not ask her name. He did not ask who she was. He already knew, I think.

FLAG: Individual entered facility under undocumented status. No employment record. No visitor log entry.
FLAG: Referral to compliance division — PENDING.
FLAG: Escorting guard filed no report following this incident.

fragments.title: Voss Memo — Case Briefing
transcript: Operator. You have been assigned Case 01.
The subject is a security guard designated VALE-7.
A data breach occurred during his assigned shift.
Surveillance footage covering the relevant window is corrupted.
Your task is to reconstruct his whereabouts and render a verdict.
You will be provided with evidence fragments across six checkpoints.
Each fragment is to be reviewed carefully before notation.
Notation is mandatory at every checkpoint.
Your entries are logged, timestamped, and retained as part of the audit record.
They will be cross-referenced with your final verdict.
Language matters. Framing matters. What you choose to emphasise is noted.
Director Voss will be reviewing your log.
Not just for what you conclude.
